subject: DPA: Data location, backup retention & secure deletion — requested redlines
messages:
From: Rachel Brown <rachel.brown@finbank.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: FinBank Legal <legal@finbank.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 08:15:00 +0100
Subject: DPA questions: EU residency + deletion windows

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the quick demo last week — the team liked the latency profile. Our legal and infosec teams are reviewing the DPA and have a handful of targeted asks before we can proceed to procurement:

1) Data residency: We need confirmation that FinBank customer data (including embeddings and logs) can be processed and stored only within EU regions (no cross-border replication to the US) unless we give explicit consent.

2) Backups & retention: Please provide exact retention windows for primary data and backups. Infosec expects a maximum of 90 days for any backups containing customer data, with the ability to remove backups on request.

3) Secure deletion: We need a clear description of deletion semantics — when a deletion request is submitted, what is the typical time-to-delete for primary stores and for backups? What guarantees do you provide about overwriting vs. logical deletion?

4) Key management: Can keys for EU data be customer-managed (KMS/HSM) so that we can revoke access if needed?

I've attached our annotated questionnaire and a redline excerpt from Legal for context. Can your team propose concrete DPA clause text for the three items above?

Rachel
Legal Ops — FinBank

Attachment stubs: FinBank_DPA_questions_0626.pdf (pdf), redline_v1_DPA.docx (docx)
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Rachel Brown <rachel.brown@finbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA questions: EU residency + deletion windows

Hi Rachel,

Appreciate the clear list — that helps. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Karthik (security) to provide suggested contractual language and the technical side of deletion/backups. High-level responses below while they draft the clauses:

- Residency: We support EU-only processing. For Hosted API customers we can restrict processing to EU regions and disable cross-region replication for customer datasets. If you require stronger isolation (no co-tenancy), we can discuss Dedicated or Private deployment options.

- Backups: Primary data (hot storage) is available for up to 30 days by default for operational purposes; backups are retained for up to 90 days in encrypted form. We can add a clause to proactively remove backup copies upon written request; timeline depends on the backup cycle.

- Deletion: Typical workflow: immediate logical deletion from primary stores within 24 hours of a validated request, and secure wipe from replicas within 30–90 days depending on backup rotation. We provide attestation of deletion upon request. We will detail overwrite vs. cryptographic key destruction options in the proposed clause.

- KMS: We support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) in our EU regions; we can add an explicit clause that key revocation results in inability to decrypt any retained copies.

Marissa/Karthik — Can you propose redline text for (1) region restriction, (2) backup retention & removal on request, and (3) deletion assurances (including key destruction option)? Also flag any technical limits (e.g., snapshot windows) so we don't promise impossible timelines.

Thanks,
Vivek
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, Rachel Brown <rachel.brown@finbank.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA questions: EU residency + deletion windows

Hi all — draft clause language below. I kept it concise so Legal at FinBank can drop it into their redline tool. If FinBank prefers different wording we can iterate.

1) Data residency (proposed DPA clause):
"Customer Data shall be processed and stored solely within Customer-designated EU data centers/regions. Redwood shall not replicate, transfer, or make Customer Data available outside the European Union without Customer's prior written consent, except to the extent necessary to comply with applicable law; Redwood will notify Customer promptly if required to transfer data by law and will seek to limit scope to the minimum necessary."

2) Backup retention & removal (proposed DPA clause):
"Redwood shall retain backups and system snapshots containing Customer Data for a maximum period of ninety (90) days. Upon Customer's written request, Redwood shall schedule removal of all backup copies containing Customer Data and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to remove such backups no later than the end of the subsequent backup retention cycle (not to exceed ninety (90) days from the date of request). Redwood will provide Customer with written confirmation when backup removal has completed."

3) Secure deletion & attestations (proposed DPA clause):
"Upon Customer's verified deletion request, Redwood shall: (a) remove Customer Data from primary production stores within twenty-four (24) hours; (b) ensure that any remaining copies in transactional caches are cleared as soon as operationally feasible; and (c) schedule deletion of Customer Data contained in backups/snapshots in accordance with the Backup retention & removal clause. At Customer's election, Redwood will either (i) overwrite or cryptographically erase Customer Data and provide an attestation of secure deletion, or (ii) destroy relevant encryption keys (if Customer's data is encrypted with Customer-managed keys) to render the data irretrievable. Redwood will provide written attestation within thirty (30) days of completion of the secure deletion process."

Notes:
- The 24-hour logical delete for primary stores is achievable for typical accounts, but full removal from all backups depends on snapshot schedules; we should avoid guaranteeing instantaneous wipe of immutable backups.
- For customers requiring stricter controls we can propose Private deployment or contractual carve-outs for dedicated storage with shorter backup cycles.

I attached a cleaned redline (redline_v1_DPA.docx) that incorporates this text. Karhik, can you confirm the technical feasibility and whether we should offer a shorter attestation window for managed key scenarios?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, Rachel Brown <rachel.brown@finbank.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 14:45:00 +0100
Subject: Re: DPA questions: EU residency + deletion windows

Rachel and team — technical notes and suggested clarifications to the draft language from an infra/security perspective:

- Residency enforcement: We can enforce region-only processing for Hosted API customers by routing requests to EU-only regions and disabling cross-region replication for customer datasets; however, ephemeral telemetry/metrics aggregated at the service level may be collected in US telemetry clusters for platform operations unless we agree to exclude FinBank on a per-contract basis. If FinBank requires absolute prohibition of any telemetry leaving EU, we should add that as an explicit requirement and discuss additional costs.

- Backup removal timeline: Our backup cadence for the EU cluster is daily snapshots with a rolling 90-day retention. When FinBank requests removal, we schedule the backup purge on the next snapshot truncation and then perform verification. In practice that means removal may occur within 24–72 hours if the relevant snapshot is still within the current retention window, or up to the end of the applicable retention cycle (<=90 days) if the snapshot is older. I recommend we keep the 90-day max and offer to prioritize FinBank's purge at operational cost.

- Secure deletion semantics:
  * Primary stores: logical delete + immediate removal of indexing records -> effective 24 hours for availability layer; underlying object storage deletion is subject to eventual consistency and GC cycles.
  * Backups: immutable snapshot deletion occurs on snapshot lifecycle purge. We can provide cryptographic erase via key destruction if the data was encrypted with customer-managed keys.

- KMS: We fully support BYO-KMS (AWS KMS EU keys or customer HSM). Key revocation will make data unreadable; we can provide deletion attestation faster in this mode since we can rely on key destruction as proof.

Proposed operational addendum (short):
"Operational note: For EU-residency customers, Redwood will: (i) configure tenant routing to EU-only processing endpoints; (ii) disable cross-region replication for Customer Data; (iii) maintain daily snapshots with a rolling 90-day retention; and (iv) upon Customer request, prioritize backup purge and provide attestation. Where Customer elects BYO-KMS, Redwood will support key destruction as a method of cryptographic erasure and will provide confirmation of key destruction within five (5) business days of request."

Let me know if FinBank wants a guaranteed shorter maximum for backups; we can model a dedicated retention policy for a Dedicated/Private deployment.

— Karthik
Principal Security Engineer — Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is very helpful and much clearer than the initial draft. A few follow-ups from Legal:

1) The residency clause is acceptable as drafted, with one small tweak: replace "European Union" with "European Economic Area and United Kingdom" to cover our EEA/UK footprint.

2) For backups, Legal wants the phrase "commercially reasonable efforts" replaced with a firm commitment to schedule removal at the next backup cycle not to exceed ninety (90) days; they will accept an operational note that prioritization may incur fees.

3) For deletion attestation, FinBank will elect the BYO-KMS/key-destruction option. Please confirm the confirmation timeline: we need assurance that proof of key destruction will be provided within five (5) business days of request.

If you can produce a redline incorporating the EEA/UK change and the firm language on backup purge timing (we can live with fees for expedited purge), we can route to Procurement. Also please attach the DocuSign link when ready and include the HubSpot deal id so our procurement team can match the documentation.

Next steps requested: updated redline (incorporating EEA/UK and the backup timing language), short note confirming BYO-KMS attestation within 5 business days, and DocuSign preparation.

Regards,
Rachel Brown
Legal Ops — FinBank
